what_is_open: Construction and proof of one fully observable confidence interval with uniform coverage over null, local, smoothness-critical, and regular regimes, together with the stated regime-adaptive half-widths.
obstruction: The population Gaussianization theorem does not establish observable common-multiplier quantile consistency or anti-concentration through variance degeneracy, and the available pilot-Hessian and covariance controls do not supply that missing uniform coupling.
attempted: A population Gaussian--quadratic interval for \(d\ge1\) and an exact Brownian-bridge quadratic interval at the \(d=0\) uniform null were derived, but neither construction is fully observable and uniformly valid across the requested mixed regimes.
partial_result: For \(d\ge1\), the infeasible population interval centered at \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}\), with half-width equal to the population Gaussian--quadratic absolute quantile divided by \(n\), a vanishing bounded--Lipschitz smoothing allowance, and a Markov allowance for the corrected remainder, has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\). At \((J_y^*,J_z^*)\) its half-width is of order \[\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-2s_z/(2s_z+d)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{d/(2s_z+d)}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2.\] For \(d=0\) at the uniform null, the interval \[\left[\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}-q^0_{1-\alpha}/n,\;\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}+q^0_{1-\alpha}/n\right]\] has coverage converging to \(1-\alpha\), where \(q^0_{1-\alpha}\) is the lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt\). Neither interval resolves the requested fully observable, uniformly mixed-regime calibration.
